transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I've been feeling really down and persistently depressed for about nine months now. It just feels like a constant cloud of sadness that I can't seem to shake.

During these past nine months, have you ever experienced periods lasting several days where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or impulsive, to the point where you needed much less sleep than normal?

No, I've never experienced anything like that at all. It's actually been the exact opposite, where I feel completely exhausted and low on energy all the time. I'm constantly struggling with sleep, either having trouble falling asleep or sleeping for hours and still waking up feeling unrefreshed.

Have you experienced this constant sadness and low energy every single day for the past nine months, or have there been periods of a few weeks or months where you felt relatively like your normal self?

No, there haven't been any breaks at all. I've felt this way every single day for the entire nine months without a single moment of feeling like my old self. It's just been a constant, heavy sadness that never lifts.
Beyond the constant sadness and fatigue, have you been experiencing other symptoms like a loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy, feelings of worthlessness, or difficulty concentrating?

Yes, absolutely. I've completely lost interest in all the hobbies I used to love, and I constantly feel useless and like a burden to my family. My mind also feels so foggy that I really struggle to focus on simple things like reading or watching TV.

Would you say that the intensity of these symptoms—such as your feelings of worthlessness and loss of interest—has been severe enough to significantly interfere with your ability to work, attend school, or manage your daily responsibilities?

Yes, it has completely taken over my life and made it almost impossible to work or handle daily responsibilities. I have absolutely no motivation to start or finish even basic tasks, and my concentration is so poor that I just can't keep up. It's been a constant, exhausting struggle every day for the last nine months, which only makes me feel more worthless.

Have you also noticed any changes in your appetite or physical weight, such as eating significantly more or less than you used to, or feeling like you are moving or speaking much more slowly than usual?

No, I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my appetite or my weight. As for my movements and speech, they feel pretty normal to me, and I don't think I've been moving or speaking any slower.
